title: Narrative Voice in Classic Fiction
text:
Classic novelists often relied on a deliberate narrative voice to shape how readers perceive their characters. Many writers chose an omniscient narrator who could enter the minds of several people and comment freely on their motives. This technique allowed authors to offer moral judgements that a more limited perspective would have made impossible. Consequently, the reader's sympathy could be guided with remarkable subtlety.

Modern critics, however, have noted that the omniscient voice can feel intrusive to contemporary readers, who often prefer to draw their own conclusions. Writers of the later nineteenth century gradually turned toward free indirect style, which blends a character's thoughts with the narrator's language. This approach preserves the intimacy of personal perspective while retaining some of the narrator's authority. The result is a texture in which judgement and sympathy seem to arise from the characters themselves.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what did many writers choose?
options: A first-person narrator with no access to other minds
An omniscient narrator who could enter several minds
A narrator who was a minor character in the story
A narrator who addressed the reader only at the end

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what is free indirect style?
options: A style that blends a character's thoughts with the narrator's language
A style that removes all narration from the text
A style that is written only in dialogue
A style invented by modern critics

questions.text: What can be inferred about why the omniscient voice might feel intrusive to modern readers?
options: Modern readers tend to prefer forming their own judgements
Modern readers find long sentences too difficult
Modern readers dislike stories about families

questions.text: What does the passage imply about the advantage of free indirect style?
options: It removes the need for characters to have thoughts
It combines closeness to a character with some narrative authority
It makes the narrator disappear completely from the story
It lets authors avoid writing descriptive passages

vocabulary.definition: tending to interfere in a way that is unwelcome
feelings of care for someone else's situation

paragraph_translations: Romancistas clássicos frequentemente recorriam a uma voz narrativa deliberada para moldar a forma como os leitores percebiam seus personagens. Muitos escritores escolheram um narrador onisciente, capaz de entrar na mente de várias pessoas e comentar livremente suas motivações. Essa técnica permitia aos autores oferecer julgamentos morais que uma perspectiva mais limitada tornaria impossíveis. Consequentemente, a simpatia do leitor podia ser guiada com notável sutileza.

Críticos modernos, no entanto, observaram que a voz onisciente pode parecer intrusiva para leitores contemporâneos, que muitas vezes preferem tirar suas próprias conclusões. Escritores do final do século XIX voltaram-se gradualmente para o estilo indireto livre, que mescla os pensamentos de um personagem com a linguagem do narrador. Essa abordagem preserva a intimidade da perspectiva pessoal, mantendo parte da autoridade do narrador. O resultado é uma textura em que o julgamento e a simpatia parecem surgir dos próprios personagens.
